solid.box: length, width, height: expr; corner?: [x,y,z] | center?: [x,y,z] (numbers in mm or length expressions; default: the origin; a box placed by its center stays centred there when its size changes); operation?, touching?, targets?: [body], name?, body_name?
solid.cylinder: radius | diameter, height: expr; base?: [x,y,z] (centre of the bottom: numbers in mm or length expressions; default: the origin); axis?: X|Y|Z|[x,y,z] (default Z); references?: [{edge: [x,y,z] on a straight edge of the face it stands on, distance: expr}] (at most two, as solid.hole's: the base centre goes that far from each edge's line, in the face's plane, and follows the edges; with a numeric base only); operation?, touching?, targets?: [body], name?, body_name?
solid.fillet: edges: [[x,y,z] point on edge | {body, index}] ; radius: expr; tangent_chain?: bool (default true: each picked edge's tangent chain is rounded with it; false: exactly the picked edges); body?: the body the edges are on (without it, each point is looked up on every placed body, shown or hidden, and a point on edges of 2 bodies is refused, naming them); type?: constant|curvature (alias g2: curvature-continuous quintic between planar faces along straight edges, one planar end face at each end (including sloped ends); radius sets the equivalent circular setback, not constant curvature; exact fit only)|chord (radius is the width across)|variable (radius at the end nearest start, radius2 at the other; one end may be 0, where the round closes to the corner)|spline (the radius along the edge is a clamped B-spline from the end nearest start: radius is its first control radius, radii the rest, knots its knot vector from 0 to 1; one end may be 0); radius2?; start?: [x,y,z]; radii?: [expr, …]; knots?: [number, …]; mid?: [[position 0…1 from start, radius expr], …] (variable radii between the ends); smooth?: bool (smooth instead of straight between the radii); corner?: rolling|g2 (rolling, the default: the corners where three blended edges meet are pieces of the rolling ball's sphere, tangent to each blend; a curvature round's corners are always g2 patches, between its own sections; g2: each corner where three or more rounded edges meet, and every edge there is rounded, is set back (1.5 × the radius along each edge unless `setbacks` names it) and filled with a patch meeting the rounds and the faces round it to the second order (curvature-continuous seams, clear of the points where a round's section ends on a face), constant-radius exact fillets only, refused where it cannot be built); setbacks?: [{vertex: [x,y,z], distance: expr}, …] (corner setbacks: the corner at the vertex nearest `vertex`, where every edge meeting it is rounded, starts its patch `distance` along each of those edges from the vertex, past where the rounds would meet (past the radius at a square corner), so the rounds blend through a larger patch; one distance for all of a corner's edges; constant-radius exact fillets only; with `corner: g2`, the G2 patch's corners); turn?: mitre|swept (where two rounds turn round a sharp, straight, convex side edge square to both on a plane, such as the rounds along a boss's base at its upright edges: mitre, the default, runs them on to meet in a mitre; swept ends them at the side edge and fills the corner with their section revolved about it, a torus; swept takes type: constant, corner: rolling, no setbacks and fit: exact or reduce, and is refused with the reason where the rounds are unequal or the side edge is concave, curved or tangent); fit?: exact|reduce|taper (exact, the default: a radius too large for the geometry around the edges is refused, naming the largest that fits; reduce: where it doesn't fit it is reduced to the largest that does, one radius for edges sharing a face; the smallest used is returned as `radius_applied`, each edge's as `radii_applied: [{edge: [x,y,z], radius}]`, and noted in the feature's warning; taper: along each straight edge between planar faces where it doesn't fit, the radius follows the room there as a smooth spline, down to 0 where a face closes to a point, noted in the feature's warning)
solid.move: bodies: [names]; translate?: [x,y,z] (length exprs or numbers, applied after rotation); axis?: [x,y,z] (default: world Z with origin, else the body's component's Z, world Z at the root); about?: {edge|face: [x,y,z], body?} (the edge or round face the turn is about, kept as a reference so the turn follows it when an earlier step moves the body; axis and origin give the turn's sense and where it is now); angle?: angle expr; origin?: [x,y,z] (length exprs or numbers in world coordinates; default: the body's component's origin, the world origin at the root); matrix?: rigid row-major 3x4 or 4x4, flat or rows (instead of translate/axis/angle/origin); tolerance?: matrix rotation tolerance (default 1e-9, at most 1e-3); copy?: bool (default false; true keeps originals and transforms copies); occurrences?: [occurrence paths, root first] (only with copy: copies each component independently and transforms the copies in world space; reply lists them in occurrences); name?, body_name?, body_names?
solid.combine: target: body; tools: [body]; operation?: join|cut|intersect; touching?: separate|one_body (what a join makes of pieces that share no face: separate, the default, makes each piece that touches another only along an edge or at a point a body of its own and keeps pieces that touch nothing in one body; one_body keeps every piece in one body); keep_tools?: bool; new_component?: bool (the result goes into a new component; component_name?)
solid.chamfer: edges: [[x,y,z] | {body, index}] ; distance: expr; tangent_chain?: bool (default true: each picked edge's tangent chain is cut with it; false: exactly the picked edges); distance2?: expr (along the second face) | angle?: expr (from the first face); flip?: bool (which face is first: by default the one facing up most); body?: the body the edges are on (without it, each point is looked up on every placed body, shown or hidden, and a point on edges of 2 bodies is refused, naming them)
solid.extrude: distance: expr (or through_all: true); taper?: angle expr (positive: outward, so the far end is larger along the extrusion direction; negative: inward, so the far end is smaller); corner?: preserve_curvature|tangent|round (how a taper closes a sharp corner its offset opens: each wall continues as itself, a line's plane or an arc's cone, until it meets its neighbour; each continues straight along its end tangent; or an arc about the corner. Without it, each profile preserves curvature where every curve is a line or an arc and takes tangent where another curve has a corner, and the feature's warning says so; a corner rule given is kept, and refused where the kernel cannot build it); sketch?: id|name (default: active or last sketch); profiles?: all | [index] | [{curves: [ids]}] (the profile whose outer loop is made of exactly these curves, or pieces of them; found again on every recompute, so it follows parameter changes; islands inside are its holes; an error when no profile or several match) | [{point:[x,y]}] (index and point picks are stored by their curves when that finds the same profile; a pick on a drawn profile that reference geometry, such as the projected outline of the face the sketch is on, cuts into regions takes the whole drawn profile); exact_regions?: bool (each index or point pick is exactly the region it names, as the dialogs send); default: every drawn profile, except that a loop inside another is its hole and a loop inside that hole is material again; face?: [x,y,z] (extrude a planar body face instead of a sketch profile); faces?: [[x,y,z],…] (coplanar faces of one body); face_body?: name (whose face, where faces of several bodies meet at the point); fixed?: true (with face or faces: start on the face's plane as a fixed plane, which won't follow later changes to the face; for a face whose history can't keep an attachment, such as a converted mesh's); direction?: positive|negative|symmetric (distance is total thickness, split evenly around the start plane); convention?: total_distance|legacy_per_side (how a symmetric distance is read; default total_distance, split evenly around the start plane; legacy_per_side: the distance on each side, as older symmetric extrudes keep); distance2?: expr (Two Sides: a second distance on the side direction leaves free, the first side may be through_all or to; with direction: negative the first side goes against the normal and distance2 along it; a negative distance only turns its own side over); start_offset?: expr (along the sketch normal, also with direction: negative); to?: [x,y,z] (To Object: a face, vertex or point; to_offset?: expr past it); from?: [x,y,z] (From Object: start at that face or point; on a flat face at a slant the start follows the face, and a distance moves it along the extrusion); operation?: new|join|cut|intersect|auto (cut into a body, otherwise join existing solids; new in an empty component); touching?: separate|one_body (what a join makes of pieces that share no face: separate, the default, makes each piece that touches another only along an edge or at a point a body of its own and keeps pieces that touch nothing in one body; one_body keeps every piece in one body); targets?: [body] (Join from a face, or from a sketch on a body's face, defaults to that face's body; explicit targets or participants override); name?; body_name?; thin?: true (Thin: a wall along sketch curves instead of the profiles) with curves?: [curve ids] (open chains and closed loops, joined where they meet end to end; default: every drawn curve of the sketch), thickness: expr, side?: center|inside|outside|two_sides (a closed loop's inside is the area it encloses, an open chain's the side it bends toward, a straight line's the left of its first curve as drawn; default center), thickness2?: expr (two_sides: the thickness outside); corners are mitred, crossing walls are one
sketch.create: plane: XY|XZ|YZ (sketch x, y along world +X, +Y on XY; +X, -Z on XZ; +Y, +Z on YZ) | construction plane name or id | {origin?: [x,y,z] in mm, default [0,0,0], each a number or a length expression (an origin whose expressions name parameters is kept, and the sketch follows them when they change), x_dir, y_dir} (in world coordinates unless frame says otherwise; a named plane is the active component's own) | {face: [world x,y,z], body?: exact world body, index?: face index, path?: complete occurrence ids, fixed?: bool}; new face attachments require a unique certified source (a flat face of a sheet metal body attaches to its panel instead, in the flat pattern's coordinates), fixed:true explicitly freezes the selected plane; offset?: expr, flip?: bool | "x" | "y" (not on a face: sketch the plane from its other side, so the normal and the default extrude direction are reversed; a half turn about the plane's own x or y axis, true picks the one keeping the sketch's y axis upward; offset still moves along the unflipped normal), frame?: world (default) | component (which coordinates an explicit plane is in; the reply's `frame` says which, with a `note` when the active component is moved or turned), project_edges?: bool, activate_part?: bool (default false; on a face of a body of another component than the active one: activate that component at the picked placement first, as component.activate would, and make the sketch there; it stays active afterwards and the reply's `activated` names it), name?
sketch.text: text: string (\n breaks lines), or text_expression: the words built from text parameters (parameters.add with unit text), number parameters and quoted texts joined by + ("Label + '-L'", "'W' + Width"; a number parameter shows its value in the design's units, "85 mm", an angle in degrees, "30°"; number(Width) is the number alone and number(Width, 2) has 2 decimals): the text keeps it, its words follow the parameters (a parameter edit or a configuration row relabels it) and `exprs` returns it as `text`; at: baseline start [x,y], height?: capital height mm (default 5), angle?: deg; at's x and y, height and angle each take a number or an expression over the design's parameters as a string ("plate_width / 2", "label_size"): the text keeps the expression, follows the parameters, and returns it in `exprs`; an expression naming no parameter is the number it comes to, a bare number in one is in the design's units, font?: an installed font's family or full name, or a .ttf/.otf file path (~ and %VAR% expand; default: the built-in Liberation Sans), bold?, italic?: bool (an installed family's bold or italic face; italic without one is slanted), align?: left|center|right (the lines against `at`, or along the path), vertical_align?: baseline|top|middle|bottom (the block of lines against `at` or the path: the first line's baseline (default), its capitals' tops, halfway between those and the last line's baseline, or the bottom of the last line's descenders), letter_spacing?: extra mm between letters, line_spacing?: times the font's line distance (default 1), path?: a curve id of the sketch the baseline follows ("": none; `at` and `angle` then do not place the text; the curve becomes construction, a guide the letters stand on), reverse?: bool (the other way along the path). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)
sketch.finish: restore_marker?: bool (default true); false transfers the temporary marker directly to another editor without rebuilding the intervening timeline
file.save_mesh: path; format?: stl|3mf|3mf-tagged (default from the extension, else stl; 3mf-tagged: docs/formats/3mf-face-tags.md); bodies?: [names] (default: all); ascii?: bool (STL); slicer?: id or name from file.slicers, the program path it lists, or a program the user added under Custom… (send the saved file there, through the same steps as file.send_to_slicer: a slicer that has to be started first is waited for; may be deprecated later in favour of file.send_to_slicer or a Send to App workflow, kept for scripts); single_instance?: bool (default true; see file.send_to_slicer); quality?: standard|fine|finest (STL, OBJ and 3MF: how closely the mesh follows curved faces, a chord tolerance of 2e-4, 5e-5 or 1e-5 of each body's size; default standard); objects?: body|component (3MF only: one object per body, the default, or one object for each placed component with two or more bodies, with those bodies as its parts, so a slicer loads them as one object with parts); lay_on_print_faces?: bool (default false: each body with a print face (body.print_face) is saved laid on it; a file sent to `slicer` is laid on them whatever this says)
inspect.measure: bodies?: [names] (default all); names_only?: bool (each world body's name and its definition's, nothing measured) → closed per body; volume_mm3, center_of_mass, density_g_cm3 and mass_g only for closed, consistently oriented bodies; area, bbox and counts for all; total.open_bodies_skipped counts bodies excluded from volume/mass totals; or items: [1-2 selections] (face/edge: type, body, and point on it or index from model.faces/model.edges, or both) → length/area/volume; a face's perimeter_mm, with outer_perimeter_mm and inner_perimeter_mm on a flat face with holes; diameter, radius, circumference or arc_length/angle_deg of circles, arcs and cylinders; slot sizes; min (distance_mm, from, to), max, center_distance (centre to centre, or from an axis) and angle
